diagnostic_evidence.quote: Based on \((Dof_1) - (Dof_3)\), let \(\boldsymbol{\chi}(\phi) = (\chi_1(\phi), \ldots, \chi_{Ndof_{loc}}(\phi))\) where \(\chi_i(\phi)\) represents the \(i\)th local degree of freedom of the smooth function \(\phi\).

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete source problem (a3.5) is posed for arbitrary F=(g,f) in W = L^2 x L^2 with right-hand side b_h(F,Psi_h) = sum_E k^2 b_h^E(f,psi_h). By the given definition, b_h^E(n*phi,psi) = b^E(n Pi^0_l phi, Pi^0_l psi) + S_b^E((I-Pi^0_l)phi,(I-Pi^0_l)psi), and S_b^E is defined through the local degrees of freedom chi, which are vertex values and Gauss-Lobatto edge values of smooth functions. For a general L^2 function f the dofs chi((I-Pi^0_l)f) do not exist, so b_h(F,.) — and with it the problem (a3.5), its solution U_h^F, and the solution operators A_h, A_h^* — is undefined on the advertised input space. The proofs confirm this reading: (a3.18) explicitly keeps the term -S_b^E((I-Pi^0_l)f,(I-Pi^0_l)z_I), i.e., the stabilized form is applied to the L^2 load f. Additionally, (a3.5) uses b_h while the operator A_h is defined with the exact form b, so the two definitions of the discrete source problem are inconsistent. Because Lemma 3.3 (a3.16), Lemma 3.4 (a3.20) and Theorem 3.1 all invoke the discrete source equation with load b_h(F,.), the a priori estimates rest on an ill-defined object.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the discrete load on non-VE data without stabilization, e.g. b_h(F,Psi_h) := sum_E k^2 b^E(Pi^0_l f, Pi^0_l psi_h) (equivalently use the exact form b(F,Psi_h), as already done in the definition of A_h), and delete the corresponding stabilization terms S_b((I-Pi^0_l)f,(I-Pi^0_l)z_I) from (a3.18) and from the I'-term in the proof of Lemma 3.4; all stated bounds then hold verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete source problem (a3.5), the adjoint source problem (a3.12), the discrete solution operators A_h and A_h^*, the stability bound (a3.11), the source-problem error estimates (a3.16) and (a3.20), and consequently the eigenpair/eigenvalue estimates (a3.21)-(a3.23) and (a3.29)-(a3.31), together with the abstract's promise of 'well-posedness of the discrete source problem', are not established as written.
issues.title: Discrete load form b_h is undefined for L^2 source data
issues.why_classification: A one-line redefinition of the load (projection-only form, or the exact form already used for A_h) plus deletion of two stabilization terms makes every definition and estimate valid verbatim; no new lemma, construction or weakening of any guarantee is required.

issues.failure_explanation: After Young's inequality the gradient coefficients are (c_* - (1/gamma)c* eps_4^{-1}) and (1/gamma)(c_* - c* eps_4); both are positive only if eps_4 > c*/(gamma c_*) and eps_4 < c_*/c*. Such eps_4 exists iff c*^2 < gamma c_*^2, i.e. gamma > (c*/c_*)^2. Since c*/c_* >= 1 is fixed by the stabilization and independent of gamma, while the lemma is claimed for every 0 < 1/gamma < 1 (gamma > 1 arbitrary), the prescribed choice is vacuous whenever 1 < gamma <= (c*/c_*)^2 (e.g. gamma close to 1), so the displayed chain does not establish (a3.9) over the advertised regime. The lemma itself is true: grouping the three gradient terms gives Re(a_h(phi,phi) - (2/gamma)a_h(psi,phi) + (1/gamma)a_h(psi,psi)) = (1/gamma)Re a_h(phi-psi,phi-psi) + (1-1/gamma)a_h(phi,phi) >= (1-1/gamma)c_* sum ||grad phi_h||^2, after which the standard Young argument works for every gamma > 1.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final Young splitting of the cross term by completing the square in the a_h inner product: Re(a_h(phi,phi) - (2/gamma)a_h(psi,phi) + (1/gamma)a_h(psi,psi)) = (1/gamma)Re a_h(phi-psi,phi-psi) + (1-1/gamma)a_h(phi,phi) >= (1-1/gamma)c_* sum_E ||grad phi_h||^2, then apply Young only to the zeroth-order cross terms; (a3.9) follows for all 1/gamma in (0,1) with K sufficiently large.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete weak T-coercivity (a3.9), on which the Fredholm well-posedness of (a3.5), the stability bound (a3.11), and the V-norm estimate (a3.20) of Lemma 3.4 (and through it Theorem th3.1 and Theorem thm:added-1) are built, is not proved for 1 < gamma <= (c*/c_*)^2, so part of the advertised regime 0 < 1/gamma < 1 lacks a proof.
issues.title: Lemma 3.1's proof uses a possibly empty admissible interval for epsilon_4
issues.why_classification: A one-line, standard rearrangement (Cauchy-Schwarz/complete-the-square in the a_h inner product) restores the full lemma verbatim on the whole advertised parameter range; no new lemma, rate or scope change is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof sets the remainder 'a_h((w_pi^f,u_pi^f),(w_h,u_h)) - a((w_pi^f,u_pi^f),(w_h,u_h)) := 0'. This term is not zero in general. By symmetry of a_h^E and a^E together with (a3.6) (which requires the second argument to lie in P_l(E)) the two gradient terms and the beta k^2 term do vanish (the latter because u_pi^f in P_l is orthogonal to (I - Pi^0_l)w_h); what survives is the refractive-index term -k^2[b_h^E(n w_pi^f, w_h) - b^E(n w_pi^f, w_h)] = -k^2(n w_pi^f, (I - Pi^0_l)w_h), which is nonzero for piecewise smooth, non-piecewise-constant n. Indeed the same term appears, correctly retained and then bounded, in the immediately following display of the same proof, showing the '- 0' identification is an error. The term is only O(h^{min(l,s)+2})||grad w_h|| and hence absorbable, so the defect is in the proof step, not in the final estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the discarded term instead of discarding it: |k^2(n w_pi^f, (I-Pi^0_l)w_h)| <= ||n w_pi^f - Pi^0_l(n w_pi^f)||_0 ||(I-Pi^0_l)w_h||_0 \lesssim h^{min(l,s)+2} |w^f|_{1+min(l,s)} ||grad w_h||_0, using the elementwise projection estimate of type (a3.13) and the VEM Poincare-type bound ||v_h - Pi^0_l v_h||_{0,E} \lesssim h_E ||grad v_h||_{0,E}; treat the corresponding term in the subsequent display identically. Inequality (a3.20) then holds unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The V-norm a priori estimate (a3.20) of Lemma lem3.4 is not established as written; through (a3.26) the gap estimate (a3.21) and the eigenvalue estimate (a3.23) of Theorem th3.1, and the estimates (a3.29) and (a3.31) of Theorem thm:added-1, lose their supporting step. The stated convergence rates remain valid after the routine repair below.
issues.title: Lemma 3.4's proof treats a nonzero a_h - a consistency term as zero
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local estimate built from tools already used in the paper (the projection error (a3.13) and the VEM Poincare-type bound); every stated rate and conclusion of Lemma lem3.4 and its dependents survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Step (a3.35) bounds ||(A_h - A)U_j||_V <= C||U_j - U_{j,h}||_V + |lambda_{j,h} - lambda_j| and then drops the eigenvalue term. The justification offered is only that |lambda_{j,h} - lambda_j| is 'a small quantity compared to' the eigenspace error. Babuska-Osborn theory (Theorem 7.3 of [Ba1991]) and the paper's own estimates provide only upper bounds, |lambda_{j,h} - lambda_j| <~ h^{2min(l,s)} and ||U_j - U_{j,h}||_V <~ h^{min(l,s)}; no lower bound on the eigenspace error is available, and for non-selfadjoint compact operators the eigenvalue and eigenfunction errors are in general of the same first order, so the claimed domination does not follow. Consequently estimate (a3.31), which is obtained by inserting (a3.35) into (a3.34), is not established as stated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the eigenvalue term: conclude ||(A_h - A)U_j||_V <~ ||U_j - U_{j,h}||_V + |lambda_{j,h} - lambda_j| and insert this into (a3.34); using |lambda_{j,h} - lambda_j| <~ h^{2min(l,s)} from Theorem th3.1 adds the additive term C h^{r+2min(l,s)} to the right-hand side of (a3.31), which is of higher order than the advertised L^2 rate and leaves the theorem's substantive content intact.
issues.overall_effect: Only the third displayed estimate (a3.31) of Theorem thm:added-1 is affected; it is not proven as stated. The other conclusions (a3.29) and (a3.30) are derived independently and remain valid, and no later result uses (a3.31).
issues.title: Unjustified domination of the eigenvalue error in deriving (a3.31)
issues.why_classification: A local fix (keeping one explicitly bounded extra term) preserves every conclusion of the theorem and its advertised higher-order L^2 message; the affected display is terminal and no dependent result is invalidated.
